## What it catches

A web server or application server process starting the command shell, PowerShell or a Windows script host. A web application has no reason to do that, and it is what a web shell does with every command it is sent. A web shell that only reads or writes files inside the server process is not seen.

```yaml
selection_parent:
  ParentImage|endswith:
  - \w3wp.exe
  - \httpd.exe
  - \nginx.exe
  - \php-cgi.exe
  - \tomcat9.exe
selection_child:
- Image|endswith:
  - \cmd.exe
  - \powershell.exe
  - \pwsh.exe
  - \cscript.exe
  - \wscript.exe
- OriginalFileName:
  - Cmd.Exe
  - PowerShell.EXE
  - pwsh.dll
  - cscript.exe
  - wscript.exe
condition: selection_parent and selection_child
```

- fires: `IIS worker starting cmd.exe`
- fires: `Apache starting powershell.exe`
- fires: `nginx starting pwsh.exe`
- fires: `PHP CGI starting cscript.exe`
- fires: `Tomcat starting wscript.exe`
- fires: `Tomcat starting cmd.exe, event without a version resource`
- fires: `PHP CGI starting powershell.exe, event without a version resource`
- fires: `nginx starting pwsh.exe, event without a version resource`
- fires: `Apache starting cscript.exe, event without a version resource`
- fires: `IIS worker starting wscript.exe, event without a version resource`
- quiet: `IIS worker compiling a page`
- quiet: `Apache starting a worker of its own`
- quiet: `nginx starting the PHP gateway`
- quiet: `a user opening a command shell from the desktop`
- quiet: `the service manager starting the IIS worker`

## False positives

- Web applications built to run system commands, such as deployment panels and some monitoring pages
- CGI scripts written as batch or PowerShell files

## What it does not see

- A web shell that works inside the server process and starts no child
- Web servers whose process has another name than the five listed
- A shell started through an intermediate program the server launches first

## First checks

- Read the child's command line and find the web request at the same second in the access log
- List files written under the web root in the days before
- Check what the child process started and which addresses it contacted
